issues: The Nobel Prize of 1962 was shared with Maurice Wilkins, who is not mentioned.
"a new strained" is a misprint for "strand". Free nucleotides are actually in the nucleus (nucleoplasm) during DNA replication, not the cytoplasm; kept as printed.

In standard biology the centromeres divide at the start of anaphase, not in metaphase, and interphase is not a "resting" phase (DNA replicates then); kept as printed. "any two mitotic division" is kept as printed.

The figure shows a fourth, unlabelled stage between Prophase and Metaphase (prometaphase) and labels the second and third cells "centromeres"; the arrangement is kept. The cleavage furrow described occurs in animal cells; plant cells form a cell plate instead.
"Nuclear membrane disappear" and "coiling … take place" are kept as printed.
Sister chromatids are identical copies of one chromosome; calling them "one maternal and the other paternal" is incorrect (that describes homologous chromosomes). Kept as printed.
The caption runs "redblood" together; kept as printed.

The terms "Mongolism" and "mental retardation" are outdated and considered offensive; they are kept only because they are printed in the book. The modern terms are Down syndrome and intellectual disability.
